A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SurpMark. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original detection experiments, sensitivity analyses, throughput measurements, and appendix evaluations of paraphrasing and R-Detect.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds benchmark evaluations, ablations, distribution-shift tests, and statistical analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain proxy-model surprisals, shared k-means quantization, first-order transition matrices, the N/n mixing weight, and the thresholded GJS difference. Expanded methodological explanations and the new zero-threshold study do not establish a changed detector procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds DAIGT evaluation with more than 15 generators and Dolly human-response evaluation. DetectRL, already evaluated in v1, gains explicit mixed-domain, mixed-generator, cross-reference, and corrupted-input scenarios. RAID coverage from v1 Appendix A3.2.5 is removed; the original English, Chinese, and German coverage otherwise remains.

E2.justification: V2 adds Binoculars and FourierGPT and extends R-Detect to the main and per-dataset comparisons, expanding those comparator sets from 10 to 13 methods. V1 evaluated R-Detect only in a separate DetectRL/RAID comparison, which is removed rather than merely relocated.

E3.justification: New protocols include TPR at 1% and 5% FPR, F1 comparisons at fixed versus test-set-optimal thresholds, controlled decoding sweeps, larger proxy models, and white-box comparisons. Appendix B also adds Markov-order experiments controlling reference size and test length. The retained main experiments still specify 300 reference and 150 test samples per class.

E4.justification: V2 adds alternative-quantizer, unigram-versus-transition, GJS-versus-L1/L2, threshold, and decoding ablations. It substantially expands robustness testing and adds analyses of marginal versus transition signals and possible pretraining exposure. Existing bin-count, length, proxy-model, and T5-paraphrasing analyses remain.

E5.justification: Appendix E.2.3 adds targeted Shapiro-Wilk tests with p-values and empirical-versus-theoretical variance estimation. The existing three-random-test-set averaging and uncertainty reporting remain; additional result rows do not establish an increased run count.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive comparator, robustness, ablation, and statistical results while retaining SurpMark's matched main-table scores. XSum/Llama-3.2-3B baseline values are revised, including LogRank AUROC from 94.87 to 59.35 in v1 Table 6 versus v2 Table 15. The HC3 score histogram switches from OpenQA to psychology, and v1's aggregate DetectRL/RAID results disappear.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 and Appendix B.2 add a formal relative-entropy-rate treatment of Markov approximation, deriving the incremental order gain through conditional mutual information. The original discretization bounds, N^(1/5) scaling, GJS/likelihood-ratio proposition, and normality proof remain; the normality theorem moves to Appendix D as Theorem D.14.

C1.justification: V2 frames the theoretical contribution as bin-scaling guidance under an idealized Markov approximation, qualifying v1's optimal-bin wording while retaining the detector and normality results. The reported reference-cost advantage also narrows from 5–5,000 times to 5–50 times in the main-results discussion.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations based on transition sparsity, marginal-versus-transition divergence, and possible pretraining-related false positives. It explicitly limits the Markov approximation and interprets theoretical variance as a conservative scale rather than precise finite-sample prediction. However, the new threshold discussion in Appendix E.2.13 reverses the score-sign interpretation given by Equation 2.

D1.justification: Appendix E.1 newly documents the 150-word input filter, 100–200-token generation, pairwise length matching, and model-family decoding defaults. New analyses provide attack prompts and threshold procedures, while v1's detailed R-Detect implementation discussion is removed. These disclosures do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations and discussion for Binoculars, FourierGPT, Gray's approximation theory, Dolly, and pretraining-exposure research. RAID and Khandelwal's context-modeling reference disappear. The central positioning relative to global statistics, likelihood-free testing, and R-Detect remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, methodological explanation, and analysis narrative are substantially revised. Related work becomes a concise introduction subsection plus Appendix C; theoretical material is redistributed, experiments gain a new organization, and explicit limitations are introduced. These changes extend beyond simply inserting additional results.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column layout, with figures and tables resized and rearranged. Main comparison tables gain baseline rows, numerous analytical tables are introduced, and the old R-Detect table is removed. V1 Figure 6 is separated into throughput and non-English figures in v2.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens support for practical use by explicitly testing reference-domain mismatch and corrupted inputs, important gaps in v1's evaluation. Component ablations, quantitative checks of Markov adequacy and normal approximation, and clearer generation details make the method's evidence and limitations more assessable. These gains outweigh the removed RAID comparison and localized inconsistencies, particularly the reversed score-sign explanation in Appendix E.2.13; the improvement does not depend on higher retained benchmark scores.
